title: Design System: Mac Pulse
platformNote: Native macOS app (SwiftUI + AppKit). It has no web surface: the component html/css below are approximations written so this panel has something faithful to render. The source of truth is App/Sources/Components.swift.

ink.note: Alpha-based so it composes over any surface in either appearance.

display.purpose: The page title each section draws for itself; the window title bar is hidden.

headline.purpose: The headline figure on a summary card.

title.purpose: Section headings, hardware name trailing in Ink Secondary.

label.purpose: Statistics-rail rows, legends, key/value pairs. Dominant size on a dense page.

caption.purpose: Units, the 'vs 5m avg' qualifier, chart footnotes.

extensions.shadowsNote: Deliberately empty. Mac Pulse uses no shadows; depth is a tonal step plus a 0.5pt hairline at 60% opacity. See the Flat Face Rule.
extensions.motionNote: The app ships no animation. Live data redraws each tick; a crossfade would fight the reading. Anything added later must convey state and honour Reduce Motion.

breakpoints.name: dashboard-min
breakpoints.note: Window minimum. Summary cards wrap two-up here; rails stay beside their charts.

breakpoints.name: rail-wrap
breakpoints.note: Below this a chart and its statistics rail stack instead of sitting side by side.

oklchRampBands.note: Stepped shades walk away from their background. Every step holds >=3:1 against its own surface; asserted by ShadeRampTests.

components.name: Metric Card
components.description: Summary card: tinted symbol and title, optional Health badge, headline figure with trend delta, sparkline, caption at full width. Approximation of MetricCard in Components.swift.

components.description: Label left, value right in monospaced digits. A row whose value is nil is omitted entirely rather than dashed. Approximation of StatRail.

components.name: Health Badge
components.description: The only component that changes colour with state: text in the Health tint over the same tint at 15%. Approximation of HealthBadge.

components.name: Navigation Button
components.description: Two only: one prominent action per page (Run Diagnostics) and a small bordered button for going elsewhere (View History). A plain button styled as a clickable row is forbidden - it has no hover or focus ring.

components.name: Chart Empty State
components.description: Before two samples exist the grid stays visible and one line names what is coming. A skeleton, never a spinner, and it distinguishes 'not yet' from 'never'.
components.html: CPU usage appears within a few seconds.

narrative.overview:
Mac Pulse is not a dashboard that decorates telemetry; it is an instrument that keeps the record. The interface exists to answer three questions in order - what is happening, when did it start, what is likely causing it - and every visual decision serves that sequence. Readings are dense, unemotional and timestamped. Colour marks an event, not a mood.

The system is deliberately built from macOS's own materials: Apple's system colors, SF Pro at stock text styles, stock controls. It owns no typeface and no palette. That is the point - a figure the app prints should be checkable against Activity Monitor, and a control should behave the way every other Mac control behaves. Identity comes from what is shown and what is refused, not from custom chrome.
keyCharacteristics: Flat surfaces, hairline borders, no shadows anywhere
One tint per metric family, stepped in OKLCH when a chart needs parts
Status colour reserved for Health Level; never decorative
Monospaced digits on every figure that changes
Native controls only - hover, focus and keyboard come from the system
A value this Mac cannot report is absent, never dashed

rules.name: The One Job Rule
rules.body: A tint means exactly one metric family. If a chart needs several parts of one family, step the same tint with MetricStyle.shade(_:of:) - never reach for a second hue. Rainbow series are forbidden.

rules.name: The Status Reserve Rule
rules.body: Green, orange and red carry Health Level and nothing else. A metric is never coloured by how alarming its value is; it is coloured by what it measures.

rules.name: The Away-From-Background Rule
rules.body: Stepped shades must walk away from the surface they sit on: darker on light, lighter on dark. Every step holds >=3:1 against its own background, asserted by tests.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Multi-word labels are sentence case. Acronyms keep their case, and names the machine supplies keep theirs.

rules.name: The Stable Digit Rule
rules.body: Any number that updates carries monospacedDigit(). A figure that reflows while you read it is a bug.

rules.name: The Flat Face Rule
rules.body: No shadow, no blur, no glass. If a surface needs to stand out it gets the hairline and the tonal step - that is the whole vocabulary.

rules.name: The Stock Control Rule
rules.body: If AppKit or SwiftUI ships the affordance, use it. A custom row that merely looks clickable loses hover, focus ring and keyboard reachability.

rules.name: The Nil Row Rule
rules.body: Components render String? and drop nil rows. Nothing displays an em dash for a value the machine cannot report.

dos: Do take tints from MetricStyle and step them with shade(_:of:). One tint per family, always.
Do keep status colour for Health Level alone - green/orange/red mean a state, never a category.
Do set monospacedDigit() on every figure that updates.
Do hide a row whose value this Mac cannot report - absence is the honest signal.
Do write multi-word labels in sentence case, and keep the machine's own words exactly as the machine gives them.
Do verify both appearances on screen. A ramp that reads well on dark can walk into a white background.
Do use stock controls so hover, focus and keyboard come from the system.
Do keep every meaningful graphic at >=3:1 against its background, and print the value beside it.
donts: Don't ship gamer/RGB monitoring skin cues: neon gradients, animated gauges, glowing rings, carbon-fibre texture.
Don't fall back to Activity Monitor's blandness - unstyled tables with no hierarchy answer nothing at a glance.
Don't build the SaaS dashboard template: hero metric tiles with gradient accents, identical card grids, decorative illustrations, purple-blue gradients.
Don't go alarmist red-everywhere. Warning colour for routine variation trains the user to ignore the one that matters.
Don't add shadows, blur or glass. If it looks lifted, it is wrong.
Don't nest a card inside a card.
Don't introduce a second hue to separate parts of one metric. Step the tint, and draw the edge.
Don't show a dash, a zero, or an estimate where a real reading is unavailable.
Don't animate live data. Motion must convey state; the app ships none, and anything added later must honour Reduce Motion.
